content.text: That message comes from the chat session’s busy handler: your follow-up hit a session that was still running. I’m checking the browser/session boundaries to confirm how separate users run alongside each other.

Bro, **that means your follow-up interrupted the active turn in that Slack thread. It does not mean Clanker has one browser slot for the whole workspace.**

Your “let’s try again” reply reached a conversation still marked busy, so the [busy handler](/Users/tanishqpalandurkar/Projects/yyot/hermes/gateway/run_busy.py:827) requested an interruption to handle your retry.

- **Separate conversations:** run concurrently. The current gateway has [10 agent worker slots](/Users/tanishqpalandurkar/Projects/yyot/hermes/gateway/run.py:60).
- **Same shared Slack thread:** shares one conversation, so follow-ups can interrupt its active turn, including another person replying there.
- **Browser sessions:** belong to individual users; each browser session accepts one active browser task at a time.

We already [verified two real Slack users browsing concurrently through one gateway](/Users/tanishqpalandurkar/Projects/yyot/verification/evidence/2026-10-04-one-gateway-two-users.md:14), with **29 seconds of overlap**. That used the earlier local browser setup; simultaneous runs on the current hosted provider still need live verification.

The message describes **conversation interruption**, not workspace-wide serialization.
